en: I get all sticky at work every day.
Even a bath won't get it off.
You're a real odd one, old man.
Since you're here, want to work with me?
Ahaha, kidding, kidding, it's a joke.
You can't do it in fancy clothes like those.
At work, the boss and older lads scold me,
and at home Mum nags me, tired from work.
But I don't really mind that stuff, you know.
Have you got a family, old man?
Guess not. You look so carefree.
But I bet a family makes you way happier.
Coming! Huh?
Who are you? My mother is out right now.
Please come back later.
Old man... you here to sell me something?
I'm just a kid, so I haven't got any money.
Old man, are you a policeman or a detective?
Let me help too! That'd be brilliant.
I don't think my mum would be much help.
Who wants to hear a middle-aged lady moan?
Hello, old man. Come on in.
It's a mess, but want some tea?
Though when I make tea, it smells of glue,
or so Mum grumbles.
You can come again if you like.
Oh dear, I'm sorry, sonny.
...Still, "old man"? That's harsh.
Calling me "sonny" is ruder, mister!
I've already got a job, you know.
I was just on my way to work.
Oh, I'm so busy.
Honestly, walking around there is dangerous,
mister.
You're right, I'll be careful.
Good luck with your work.
You sound just like my mum.
"Mister" doesn't suit you after all.
See you, old man!
Oh dear, back to "old man" again...
Oh, sorry. It's "mister", isn't it?
note: Follows slice 060 #4833 'Aren't you going to work, old man?'.

en: Good morning, old m... mister.
Hey, mister. Taking it easy again today?
I bet you're from a good family, mister.
"Old man", is it? That's harsh.
Aren't you on your way home from school?
School? That's for folks with time
and money. Nothing to do with me.
It's "mister", right? Good evening.
Huh? But wait, do you even work, mister?
Hey, mister. Doing all right?
Ugh... What a smell.
The smell is so foul, I forgot why I came.
I'll come back another time. Bye.
You again, mister?
You're a real odd one, mister.
Have you got a family, mister?
But I'm not jealous or anything.
'Cause having a family is way happier,
if you ask me.
Mister, are you a policeman or a detective?
Hello, mister. Come on in.
Even a child this small has to work...
Humans are admirable. They get by on
their own strength alone...
We can't exist without humans.
How ironic...
Give this servant any order you wish...
note: After '{NAME}, my master...' (M2#0); starts a new sentence.

en: I get the odd cut now and then,
but bruises are rare. Can't recall how.
Master, tell me what you require.
Somehow I just can't sleep well at night.
And my body's worn out, too. Strange, that.
Morning! You're an early riser, aren't you?
Ah, good morning.
You're not from around here.
Never seen your face before.
I'm Malcolm. I run the butcher's over there.
And you?
Pleased to meet you, Malcolm.
